fetch_sources_non_idempotency.finding: lab_data.fetch_sources is NOT idempotent, and its own write-once guard makes the second invocation FAIL with WriteOnceViolation.
fetch_sources_non_idempotency.mechanism: the manifest records each source's `origin` path. On the first call the files are found in CACHE_SEARCH_DIRS, so origin names the cache. The call then COPIES them into dest. On a second call _find_cached finds them in dest first, so origin names dest. Different bytes for the same inputs and the same intent.
fetch_sources_non_idempotency.not_repaired_here: fetch_sources is live_ab harness code pinned by harness_file_sha256. Changing it moves that digest. Reported, not silently patched.
fetch_sources_non_idempotency.s2_provenance_note: mbpp_full resolved from an EXTERNAL cache dir, not from the repo. roster_mode EXT depends on that file, so its origin is recorded rather than assumed.
fetch_sources_non_idempotency.severity: the SCIENTIFIC content is stable -- every sha256, byte count, revision and stratum is identical between runs. Only a provenance path string moves.
fetch_sources_non_idempotency.who_it_bites: anyone re-running preparation against an already-populated sources dir, including a resumed or repeated freeze attempt.
fetch_sources_non_idempotency.workaround_used: this stage READS the existing write-once manifest instead of regenerating it. Nothing was deleted; the original manifest stands.

why_stage_1_stops_here.text: Any task whose reference solution does not pass verify() twice in a row inside the Seatbelt sandbox on the trial machine UNDER THE LOAD REGIME OF THE TRIAL (a 1,024-token generation running on the coder server during the sweep), or whose reference verification takes more than half of the 5 s verifier wall limit in either run.
why_stage_1_stops_here.why_it_blocks: reference_timeout is a WALL-TIME threshold (0.5 x 5 s = 2.5 s) and wall time depends on load. Sweeping on an idle machine makes the verifier faster, so FEWER tasks cross the threshold, so MORE survive, so the roster is LARGER. That roster would have the right shape, right format and plausible counts and would be WRONG. write_roster is write-once, so it could not be corrected afterwards.
